title: Effect of aerobic exercise on cancer-associated cognitive impairment: A proof-of-concept RCT
intervention_description: 24-week aerobic exercise: 150 min/wk MVPA, 2x supervised 45-min gym sessions + 2x home sessions (30-min). Intensity 60-80% HRR. Delayed-exercise usual-lifestyle control.
significant_findings: TMT-A: adj diff -14.2s p=0.01 partial_eta_sq=0.35 (processing speed SIGNIFICANT)
VO2peak: adj diff +3.6 ml/kg/min p<0.01 partial_eta_sq=0.43 (fitness confirmed)
null_findings: FACT-Cog PCI p=0.44 (subjective cognitive complaints, null)
HVLT Total Recall p=0.52 (episodic memory, null)
Animal fluency p=0.15 (verbal fluency, trend only)
FACT-F fatigue p=0.18 (clinically meaningful +6.3 but not significant)

fmri_findings.interpretation: EX showed less brain activation (greater efficiency) in conflict monitoring regions; consistent with neural efficiency hypothesis

limitations: Small sample size (n=19): underpowered for most outcomes except TMT-A
Only postmenopausal breast cancer on aromatase inhibitor — narrow generalizability
3-year post-treatment window may include heterogeneous cognitive trajectories
extraction_notes: FIRST aerobic exercise RCT with cognitive primary outcomes in breast cancer survivors. TMT-A is strongest evidence. fMRI data in subset only (n=14). FACT-F TOI 113.0 (out of 160) not 52 — using trial-specific reporting of FACT-F total score which differs from standard FACT-F subscale. Verify FACT-F scoring.
